basic_identification.full_title: Methods of Test for Plastic Flooring and Wall Tiles (Second Revision) (प्लास्टिक फर्श और दीवार टाइलों के परीक्षण की पद्धतियां (दूसरा पुनरीक्षण))
basic_identification.sector_category: Civil Engineering / Flooring, Wall Finishing and Roofing (approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Flooring, Wall Finishing and Roofing Sectional Committee, CED 5, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Flooring, Wall Finishing and Roofing Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard prescribes the laboratory testing methods for carrying out physical, mechanical, thermal, and chemical tests on flexible PVC flooring, PVC asbestos floor tiles, and polystyrene wall tiles to evaluate their quality, performance, and durability.

version_status_and_amendments.year_first_published: 1965 (originally adopted by the Indian Standards Institution in 1965, revised to its first revision in 1974, and adopted as this active second revision in 1986)
version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No active amendments have been issued on this copy (NIL on this copy).

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Random sampling and randomization procedures (First Revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Outlines mathematical randomization procedures for drawing representative inspection samples from manufactured flooring consignments.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Reagent grade water (Fourth Revision)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Specifies purity parameters for reagent water utilized for preparing laboratory blanks, standardizations, and water-absorption tests.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Specification for ethyl acetate for cosmetic industry
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Provides chemical purity specifications for ethyl acetate utilized in ply-adhesion wet lamina extraction.

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Standardises the mathematical rounding of observed or calculated test dimensions, thickness readings, and test forces to determine code compliance.

allied_standards.title: Specification for unbacked flexible PVC flooring (first revision)
allied_standards.relevance: The master product specification for unbacked vinyl sheets and tiles whose physical, thermal, and chemical performance is verified using the testing protocols of IS 3464.

allied_standards.title: Specification for PVC asbestos floor tiles (first revision)
allied_standards.relevance: Regulates semi-flexible tiles containing asbestos fibers, which are subjected to impact, deflection, and indentation testing under IS 3464.

allied_standards.title: Code of practice for laying of flexible PVC sheet and tile flooring
allied_standards.relevance: Directs the on-site laying, sub-floor drying, adhesive application, and conditioning of flexible PVC flooring conforming to IS 3462 and tested per IS 3464.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice on Occupational Safety and Health Audit
allied_standards.relevance: Directs safety audits of industrial work environments. On-site audits physically inspect commercial flooring for slip resistance, structural bubbling, or corner curling, which represent serious pedestrian trip hazards.

allied_standards.title: Occupational Health and Safety Management System (First Revision)
allied_standards.relevance: Unifies risk mitigation, mandating regular physical maintenance and hazard inspections of access routes to ensure they remain flat and slip-free.

allied_standards.title: Drinking Water — Specification
allied_standards.relevance: Ensures that high-purity water utilized in water-absorption testing remains free of mineral scaling residues that could bias dry weight measurements.

allied_standards.title: Code of Practice for General Steel Construction
allied_standards.relevance: The master structural steel code in India, regulating support framing and steel decks which must be designed to remain rigid. Excessive structural deflection in steel-framed floors causes shear failure in adhesive-bonded tile overlays.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Methods of Test / Technical Laboratory Guidelines (Civil Engineering Department / Flooring and Wall Finish)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 3464 is an analytical testing standard rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry an individual physical 'ISI Mark' product stamp on its own. However, compliance with its sampling, thermal aging, and mechanical testing protocols is strictly required in laboratory accreditation audits (under NABL ISO/IEC 17025:2017) and public sector raw material procurement audits by the CPWD, state PWDs, Indian Railways, and the Ministry of Defence.

requirements.detail: Specifies squareness tests on tiles to ensure they have perfect 90° corners, with lateral deviation restricted to a maximum tolerance of ≤ 0.15 mm to prevent joint opening during laying.

Specimens must be heated in laboratory drying ovens (typically at 80°C) to quantify thermal shrinkage or expansion, restricting linear dimensional changes to a maximum of 1.75 percent (or 0.6 percent for premium grades).

Lifting of the corners of specimen tiles under environmental conditioning is measured in mm using dial indicators, requiring that the flooring show no sign of curling to prevent pedestrian trip hazards.

Measures the depth of depression when the flooring is subjected to a concentrated vertical load via a standard indentor tip. For flexible PVC flooring, the depth is measured at exactly 1 minute (typically < 0.65 mm) and 10 minutes (typically 0.85 mm).

Evaluates the material's elastic recovery. After a concentrated load is applied for a set period and then removed, the remaining permanent depression (residual indentation) is measured, with the maximum allowable limit strictly capped at 0.10 mm to ensure resistance to damage from heavy furniture.

Multi-layered PVC flooring is tested for delamination. The test piece is supported vertically in ethyl acetate solvent to a depth of not more than 20 mm for exactly 45 minutes. The laminated layers are manually separated at the wetted edge, dried at 27 ± 2°C for not less than 90 minutes, and then clamped in a tensile testing machine to record the separation load of a 75 mm marked section.

Specimens are submerged in distilled water and mineral oil separately to calculate weight gain and verify low porosity, restricting water absorption to < 0.4 percent (or 0.1 percent) and oil absorption to < 0.5 percent (or 0.05 percent) by mass.
Quantifies the weight loss of the plastic flooring after oven-drying to evaluate the evaporation of plasticizers, solvents, or processing oils, preventing shrinkage and premature embrittlement.
Deflection and falling-weight impact tests are conducted on semi-flexible and asbestos-fiber tiles to verify structural flexibility and fracture resistance.
Exposes the decorative face of the flooring to household cleaners, mild acids, and alkalis, checking for surface staining, color bleeding, or chemical swelling.

All observed or calculated test and analytical values must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 3464 : 1986 (Second Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard test code prescribing laboratory testing methods for flexible PVC flooring, PVC asbestos floor tiles, and polystyrene wall tiles. Developed under the Flooring, Wall Finishing and Roofing Sectional Committee (CED 5) and reaffirmed in 2022, the standard unifies twenty-one distinct mechanical, physical, and chemical tests. These include measuring geometric squareness (within 0.15 mm), testing dimensional stability under thermal loading (within 1.75% shrinkage), verifying that flooring does not curl, measuring indentation and residual elastic recovery (residual indentation capped at 0.10 mm), and conducting ply-adhesion tests under ethyl acetate solvent exposure, ensuring long-term durability and safety across India's infrastructure and construction sectors.
